title: Zoning floor area
prompt:
A 204 ft × 196 ft lot is zoned with a maximum floor area ratio (FAR) of 6.0. The proposed building footprint is L-shaped: a 125 ft × 46 ft main block plus a separate, non-overlapping 45 ft × 38 ft wing. Every one of its 5 stories has that same footprint.
Give the proposed gross floor area, the maximum floor area the FAR allows, whether it complies ("yes"/"no"), and the margin in sq ft (allowed − proposed; negative if over).
Answer keys: "proposed_gross_floor_area" (number), "max_allowed_floor_area" (number), "complies" (string), "margin_sq_ft" (number).

title: Occupant load and egress
prompt:
A single-story tenant fit-out has these spaces. The area given for each is the one its load factor applies to (net or gross, as marked).

| Space | Area | Occupant load factor |
|---|---|---|
| Assembly — unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 3,340 sq ft (net) | 15 sq ft per occupant |
| Mercantile — sales floor | 2,860 sq ft (gross) | 60 sq ft per occupant |
| Storage / mechanical | 4,390 sq ft (gross) | 300 sq ft per occupant |

Rules for this jurisdiction: occupant load of each space = its area ÷ its load factor, rounded UP per space; the floor's occupant load is the sum. Exits required: 1 for up to 49 occupants, 2 for 50–500, 3 for 501–1,000, 4 above 1,000. Minimum total egress width at doors is 0.2 inch per occupant.
Give the total occupant load, the number of exits required, and the minimum total egress width in inches.
Answer keys: "total_occupant_load" (integer), "required_exits" (integer), "min_egress_width_in" (number).

title: Stair geometry
prompt:
Lay out a straight-run stair between floors 183 inches apart (finished floor to finished floor). The code allows a maximum riser of 7.0 in, and you will use a 11.0 in tread depth. Use the fewest risers that satisfy the maximum, all risers equal. Treads number one fewer than risers; total run is treads × tread depth.
Answer keys: "risers" (integer), "riser_height_in" (number), "treads" (integer), "total_run_in" (number).

| Week | Cash in | Cash out |

| 1 | $590,000 | $163,000 |
| 2 | — | $154,000 |
| 3 | $800,000 | $191,000 |
| 4 | — | $412,000 |
| 5 | — | $186,000 |
| 6 | $855,000 | $183,000 |
| 7 | $395,000 | $144,000 |
| 8 | — | $645,000 |
| 9 | $820,000 | $193,000 |
| 10 | — | $143,000 |
| 11 | $305,000 | $176,000 |

Closing balance = opening + cash in − cash out, carried week to week. Give the lowest closing balance, the week it occurs (the first such week if tied), and the closing balance in the last week listed.
Answer keys: "lowest_closing_balance" (number), "lowest_week" (integer), "closing_balance_final_week" (number).

title: Earthwork cut and fill
prompt:
A site is surveyed on a 25 ft grid; existing spot elevations (ft) at the grid corners are below (rows run north to south). The whole area is graded to a flat pad at elevation 104.3 ft.

| C0 | C1 | C2 | C3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 105.9 | 102.5 | 102.3 | 102.3 |
| 101.3 | 103.7 | 103.9 | 101.2 |
| 105.4 | 103.9 | 106.7 | 106.9 |
| 101.0 | 102.7 | 103.5 | 105.3 |
| 106.6 | 104.3 | 103.2 | 105.0 |

Use the grid method: for each grid cell, depth = the average of (pad − existing) at its four corners; a positive depth is fill, negative is cut; cell volume = cell area × |depth| ÷ 27 (cubic yards). Sum cut and fill separately. Give total cut, total fill, net (fill − cut) and whether the site must "import" or "export" soil to balance.
Answer keys: "cut_cy" (number), "fill_cy" (number), "net_cy" (number), "import_or_export" (string).

title: Asphalt paving tonnage
prompt:
Pave 11,730 square yards with a 2.0 in base course and a 1.5 in surface course of hot-mix asphalt. Use 110 lb per square yard per inch of compacted thickness and add 5% waste to the total. Give tons of base, tons of surface (before waste), and total tons including waste (2,000 lb per ton).
Answer keys: "base_course_tons" (number), "surface_course_tons" (number), "total_tons_with_waste" (number).

title: Gravity pipe slope and capacity
prompt:
A storm sewer runs 253 ft from an upstream invert of 105.03 ft to a downstream invert of 103.13 ft, in 18 in diameter pipe with Manning's n = 0.012. Design flow is 8.68 cfs.
Give the slope as a percent, the full-flow capacity from Manning's equation in US units (Q = 1.49/n × A × R^(2/3) × S^(1/2), with A the full area and R = D/4 for a full circular pipe), and whether capacity is at least the design flow ("yes"/"no").
Answer keys: "slope_percent" (number), "full_flow_cfs" (number), "adequate" (string).

title: Change order pricing with markups
prompt:
Price a change order for job J-1839 under these contract terms.

Self-performed work: 483 labor hours at a base wage of $72.00/hour plus labor burden of 28% of wages; material $55,100; owned equipment $3,875.
Subcontracted work: $25,300.

Markups, in this order: overhead of 12% on self-performed cost; then fee of 5% on self-performed cost plus its overhead; 7.5% markup on subcontracted work; then a bond premium of 1.5% on the total of everything above.
Give the burdened labor cost, the subtotal before bond, and the change order price.
Answer keys: "labor_cost" (number), "subtotal_before_bond" (number), "change_order_price" (number).

title: Beam bending, shear and deflection
prompt:
A simply supported beam spans 22 ft and carries a total uniform load of 1,025 lb/ft (self-weight included). Allowable bending stress Fb = 2,400 psi; E = 1,600,000 psi; the trial section has I = 1935 in⁴.
Give the maximum bending moment (ft-kips), the maximum shear (kips), the required section modulus in in³ (M ÷ Fb, with consistent units), the midspan deflection in inches under this load, and whether the deflection meets L/360 ("yes"/"no").
Answer keys: "max_moment_ft_kips" (number), "max_shear_kips" (number), "required_section_modulus_in3" (number), "deflection_in" (number), "deflection_ok_L360" (string).

title: Duct velocity and equivalent round
prompt:
A supply duct carries 6,950 CFM through a 10 in × 16 in rectangular section (inside dimensions).
Give the air velocity in feet per minute, and the diameter of a round duct with the same cross-sectional area (equal area, not equal friction), in inches.
Answer keys: "velocity_fpm" (number), "equal_area_round_diameter_in" (number).

Give the line current, and the smallest standard breaker rating that is at least 125% of that current. Standard ratings (A): 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200, 225, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000.

title: Drone survey flight plan
prompt:
Plan a drone mapping flight over a 875 m × 1332 m site at 60 m altitude. The camera's horizontal field of view across the flight line is 60°. Use 70% side overlap.
Image footprint width = 2 × altitude × tan(FOV/2). Line spacing = footprint × (1 − side overlap). Flight lines run along the 1332 m side: number of lines = ceil(width ÷ spacing) + 1. Flight distance = lines × 1332 m + (lines − 1) × spacing for the turns. The drone flies at 12 m/s and each battery gives 30 minutes of survey flight. Give the footprint width, line spacing, number of lines, flight minutes and batteries needed (rounded up).
Answer keys: "footprint_width_m" (number), "line_spacing_m" (number), "flight_lines" (integer), "flight_minutes" (number), "batteries" (integer).

Answer keys: "point1_easting" (number), "point1_northing" (number), "distance_p1_p2" (number).

title: Rebar-tying robot vs crew

A rebar-tying robot will tie a single bridge-deck mat 232 ft × 88 ft. Bars running the long way are at 10 in spacing; bars running the short way at 6 in. The first and last bar each sit 2 in in from the edges; bars per direction = floor((dimension across them − 2 × cover) ÷ spacing) + 1 (work in inches). Tie every other intersection (every other = half, rounded up). The robot ties 1,300 intersections an hour; a crew of 3 ironworkers ties 400 an hour each. Give bars each way, ties, robot hours and crew hours.
Answer keys: "bars_long_direction" (integer), "bars_short_direction" (integer), "ties" (integer), "robot_hours" (number), "crew_hours" (number).

title: Fall clearance
prompt:

Free fall = lanyard length + the distance the D-ring is above the anchor (negative when the anchor is higher; never below zero). Required clearance below the working surface = free fall + deceleration + D-ring height + safety factor. There are 8.4 ft to the level below. Give the free fall distance, the required clearance, and whether the available clearance is adequate ("yes"/"no").
Answer keys: "free_fall_ft" (number), "required_clearance_ft" (number), "adequate" (string).

title: Three-week look-ahead
prompt:
Build a three-week look-ahead for the Monday 10/05/2026 coordination meeting: the window is 10/05/2026 through 10/25/2026, both inclusive.

| ID | Activity | Start | Finish |
|---|---|---|---|
| 101 | Mobilize L3 | 10/09/2026 | 10/20/2026 |
| 102 | Excavate | 10/19/2026 | 10/21/2026 |
| 103 | Footings | 09/24/2026 | 09/30/2026 |
| 104 | Foundation walls | 11/13/2026 | 12/05/2026 |
| 105 | Underground MEP | 10/21/2026 | 10/31/2026 |
| 106 | Slab on grade L2 | 10/13/2026 | 11/03/2026 |
| 107 | Steel erection L5 | 10/28/2026 | 11/11/2026 |
| 108 | Deck & pour | 10/04/2026 | 10/09/2026 |
| 109 | Roofing | 10/19/2026 | 10/22/2026 |
| 110 | Exterior envelope L4 | 10/14/2026 | 11/12/2026 |
| 111 | MEP rough-in | 09/15/2026 | 09/22/2026 |
| 112 | Framing L3 | 10/29/2026 | 11/10/2026 |

List the activities that START inside the window, and every activity ACTIVE at any point in the window (it starts on or before the window's last day and finishes on or after its first day).
Answer keys: "starting_in_window" (array), "active_in_window" (array).

title: Embodied carbon of a take-off
prompt:
Embodied carbon (A1–A3) for a 3,374 m² building, from its material take-off and the project's chosen emission factors:

| Material | Quantity | Factor |
|---|---|---|
| CLT timber panels | 964.0 m³ | 160 kgCO₂e per m³ |
| Ready-mix concrete, 4000 psi | 218.7 m³ | 320 kgCO₂e per m³ |
| Gypsum board | 311.4 m² | 3.1 kgCO₂e per m² |
| Float glass | 115.7 t | 1,400 kgCO₂e per t |
| Structural steel sections | 247.9 t | 1,550 kgCO₂e per t |

Give the total in tonnes CO₂e, the intensity in kgCO₂e per m² of floor area, the material contributing most, and the saving in tonnes if the factor for "Float glass" is reduced by 20% (quantity unchanged).
Answer keys: "total_tCO2e" (number), "kgCO2e_per_m2" (number), "largest_contributor" (string), "saving_tCO2e" (number).

title: Energy use intensity and cost
prompt:
A 360,736 sq ft office used 2,898,400 kWh of electricity and 63,790 therms of natural gas last year. Electricity costs $0.205/kWh and gas $1.54/therm. Using 3.412 kBtu per kWh and 100 kBtu per therm, give the site energy use intensity (kBtu per sq ft per year), the annual energy cost, and cost per sq ft.
Answer keys: "site_eui_kbtu_per_sf" (number), "annual_energy_cost" (number), "cost_per_sf" (number).

title: Rooftop solar sizing and payback
prompt:
A 45,691 sq ft roof has 60% of its area usable for PV. Modules are 450 W, 23.0 sq ft each (whole modules only, round down). The site produces 1,450 kWh per kW-DC per year. Installed cost is $2.76/W-DC before a 30% incentive, and the building pays $0.217/kWh. Give the number of modules, system size in kW-DC, annual kWh, and simple payback in years (net cost ÷ annual savings).
Answer keys: "panels" (integer), "system_kw_dc" (number), "annual_kwh" (number), "simple_payback_years" (number).

title: WIP schedule and over/under billing
prompt:
A contractor's work-in-progress schedule for the month:

| Job | Contract value | Estimated total cost | Cost to date | Billed to date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kingsley High Gym | $750,000 | $628,000 | $345,500 | $370,500 |
| Harbourview Clinic | $5,960,000 | $5,395,000 | $3,754,000 | $4,446,500 |
| Mason Street Retail | $2,195,000 | $2,017,000 | $1,107,000 | $1,268,500 |
| Summit Hotel Renovation | $3,485,000 | $3,104,000 | $1,424,500 | $1,737,000 |

Recognise revenue by percentage of completion using the cost-to-cost method (cost to date ÷ estimated total cost). Over/under billing is billed to date minus earned revenue: positive is over-billed, negative is under-billed.
Give the net over/under billing across all jobs, the name of the most under-billed job (the most negative over/under figure), and that job's under-billing as a positive amount.
Answer keys: "net_over_under_billing" (number), "most_underbilled_job" (string), "most_underbilled_amount" (number).
